{{Otheruses|Ritsuryō-era government agency overseeing markets|Other uses of the term "市司"|qq=}}
'''Ichitsukasa''' (市司) was a government agency under the {{ill|Right Capital Ward Officer|ja|京職|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyōshiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11374719}} in the {{ill|Ritsuryō|en|Ritsuryō|qid=Q742460|lt=Ritsuryō system}}. It managed the markets located in the capital, with the '''Tōichitsukasa''' (東市司) under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Right Capital Ward Officer|ja|左京職|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakyōshiki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 京職|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11374719}} and the '''Saiichitsukasa''' (西市司) under the {{ill|Right Capital Ward Officer|ja|右京職|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ukyōshiki|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 京職|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11374719}}.
== History ==
During the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|qid=Q2658252|lt=Yamato period}} (Yamato court), markets such as {{ill|Tsubakiichi|ja|海石榴市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsubakiichi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 海柘榴市 (大和国)}} and {{ill|Karunoichi|ja|軽市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Karunoichi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Asuka, and {{ill|Ekaichi|ja|餌香市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ekaichi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Adokuwanoichi|ja|阿斗桑市|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Adokuwanoichi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|Kawachi Province|qid=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi Province}} were politically utilized at key transportation hubs. The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} references administrators called "Ichitsukasa" (市司) starting in the {{ill|Taika (era)|en|Taika (era)|qid=Q1077930|lt=Taika era}}, though it is unclear whether they were appointed officials or market representatives approved by the court.<ref name="market_management">Miyakawa, "Market Management under the Ritsuryō System"</ref>
With the construction of {{ill|Fujiwara-kyō|en|Fujiwara-kyō|qid=Q1196381|lt=Fujiwara-kyō}} and the enactment of the {{ill|Taihō Code|en|Taihō Code|qid=Q1059892|lt=Taihō Code}}, markets previously scattered across regions were centralized within the capital, forming the East and West Markets. The establishment of Ichitsukasa as a formal management agency is believed to coincide with this centralization. According to the {{ill|Fusō Ryakuki|en|Fusō Ryakuki|qid=Q11076282|lt=Fusō Ryakki}} and {{ill|Teiō Henki|ja|帝王編年記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Teiō Henki|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=DELETED_QID|dd=Q135550950}}, the East and West Markets were first established in {{ill|703|ja|大宝3年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taihō 3|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135550951}} (703).<ref name="market_management"/> Additionally, the markets and Ichitsukasa were exclusive to the capital. With each relocation of the capital ({{ill|capital city relocation|ja|遷都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sento|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q558566}}), the markets, Ichitsukasa, and merchants were moved accordingly.<ref name="capital_markets">Miyakawa, "Capital Markets and the East and West Markets"</ref>
Unlike in Tang China, where Ichitsukasa existed at both the central and local levels, Japan did not establish government-operated markets or Ichitsukasa in provincial areas. Instead, {{ill|Kokushi (official)|en|Kokushi (official)|qid=Q1351234|lt=Kokushi}} relied on preexisting markets created by local aristocrats or officials, including {{ill|Gunji|ja|郡司|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gunji|qq=}}, at transportation hubs.<ref name="market_management"/>
== Functions ==
Ichitsukasa supervised the East and West Markets in the capital. Its responsibilities included:
- Preventing fraud and crime in the markets.
- Managing weights and measures ({{ill|weights and measures|ja|度量衡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doryōkō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q13862405}}).
- Monitoring commodity prices.
- Procuring goods for government use when necessary.
Ichitsukasa also created price survey reports called {{ill|Kokachō|ja|估価帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokachō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. These reports, compiled every ten days (or monthly as per the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}), classified prices into three tiers: udder, middle, and lower, with further subcategories of high, medium, and low (resulting in nine levels overall). The reports were submitted to the relevant {{ill|Right Capital Ward Officer|ja|京職|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyōshiki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11374719}}, serving as a reference for fair pricing in government procurement.<ref>Mori Akihiko, "Characteristics of Ancient Japan's Value Systems and Currency," in *Studies on Japan's Ancient Currency System* (Hanawa Shobō, 2016), ISBN 978-4-8273-1283-6</ref>
The head of Ichitsukasa, the '''Ichinokami''' (市正), was originally a {{ill|Shōroku-i-jō|ja|正六位上|1=Senior Sixth Rank|lt=Senior Sixth Rank, Upper Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i-jō|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 正六位}} Rank official. However, in practice, experienced bureaucrats of the Fifth Rank, {{ill|Tokugōshō|ja|得業生|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugyōsei|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97212787}}, or {{ill|Monjōshō|ja|文章生|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monjōsei|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q97378717}} were often addointed, especially those with financial acumen. {{ill|Office of Police and Justice|lt=Office of Police and Justice|lt=Kebiishi|ja|検非違使|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kebiishi|qq=}} officials sometimes concurrently held the role to oversee market security.
== Personnel ==
* Ichinokami (市正): 1 for East and West Markets each ({{ill|Shōroku-i-jō|ja|正六位上|1=Senior Sixth Rank|lt=Senior Sixth Rank, Upper Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōroku-i-jō|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Sixth Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 正六位}} Rank).
* Ichinoyu (市佑): 1 for each market ({{ill|Jūshichii-ge|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūshichii-ge|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}} Rank).
* Ichinoreishi (市令史): 1 for each market ({{ill|Dai-shoi-jō|ja|大初位上|1=Senior Initial Rank|lt=Senior Initial Rank, Upper Grade|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dai-shoi-jō|13=User:Immanuelle/Senior Initial Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大初位}} Rank).
Additional staff:
- Clerks (史生): 2 for each market (later reduced to 1).
- Katana (価長): 5 for each market.
- Mononobe (物部): 20 for each market.
- Assistants (使部): 10 for each market (later reduced to 6).
- Stewards (直丁): 1 for each market.
